title: Everolimus + exemestane
setting: Postmenopausal HR-positive / HER2-negative advanced breast cancer
dose: Usual starting doses: everolimus 10 mg once daily and exemestane 25 mg once daily; the prescribed everolimus dose may be lower.
schedule: Both tablets are taken every day continuously. There is no planned week off. A four-week blood-test review is a monitoring interval, not a stop-and-restart treatment cycle.
administration: Take everolimus at the same time daily, consistently with food or consistently without food. Take exemestane after a meal. Swallow tablets whole with water; do not crush or chew. If a dose is missed, take the next scheduled dose without adding an extra dose.
duration: Continue while the treatment is helping and side effects remain manageable, according to the consultant plan. This advanced-disease regimen has no fixed adjuvant completion date.
indication: NCCP 00322a: postmenopausal hormone receptor-positive, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer without symptomatic visceral disease after recurrence or progression following a non-steroidal aromatase inhibitor.
purpose: Exemestane lowers oestrogen production while everolimus blocks an intracellular growth pathway that can contribute to endocrine resistance. The aim in this setting is to control cancer and delay progression.
baseline: Before starting: FBC, renal and liver profile, urea/BUN, urinary protein, blood glucose, cholesterol and triglycerides. Confirm the endocrine indication, review lung symptoms and infections, and check all medicines. Assess bone/fracture risk for the exemestane component.
ongoing: FBC, renal/liver profile, cholesterol and triglycerides every four weeks or as clinically indicated. Check fasting glucose as clinically indicated, with closer monitoring if diabetes or another medicine increases risk. Ask about mouth soreness, infection, cough/breathlessness and daily function at reviews.
heart: NCCP 00322 does not mandate routine ECG or echocardiography. Cardiac tests should follow symptoms, comorbidities and other treatments, rather than a copied HER2-treatment schedule.
bone: Exemestane can reduce bone mineral density. Review fracture risk and arrange DXA and bone protection when indicated. This regimen does not specify a single repeat-DXA interval for everyone.
urgent: Contact the oncology team promptly for new or worsening cough or breathlessness, fever or infection symptoms, mouth sores that prevent drinking/eating, severe diarrhoea or dehydration, or marked thirst and frequent urination. Severe breathing difficulty, collapse or swelling of the tongue/throat needs emergency help.
special: If everolimus is interrupted or reduced for toxicity, NCCP says exemestane may continue; the treating team must confirm the plan for each medicine. Do not stop both automatically or restart everolimus yourself. Everolimus can increase toxicity around radiotherapy and impair wound healing: agree a specific plan before radiotherapy or surgery.
contraception: This NCCP indication is postmenopausal. If pregnancy remains possible or menopause is uncertain, ask the team to confirm endocrine status and suitable contraception. Everolimus product information advises highly effective contraception during treatment and for eight weeks after it ends; pregnancy and breastfeeding are NCCP exclusions.

logistics.title: Two daily tablets, two different jobs
logistics.text: Keep a simple routine for the oral medicines and request your next supply before tablets run out. No port or pump is needed for this regimen itself.

logistics.title: Four-week review, continuous treatment
logistics.text: A blood-test or pharmacy review every four weeks does not mean a rest week. Follow the prescribed daily doses unless the team explicitly tells you to pause.

logistics.title: The first eight weeks: mouth care
logistics.text: Agree a mouth-care plan before the first dose. The team may prescribe an alcohol-free steroid mouthwash. Report soreness early, before it affects eating or drinking; use the specific prescribed directions.

logistics.title: When one medicine is held
logistics.text: Ask the team to state clearly which tablet to pause, whether exemestane should continue, what needs to recover and who will authorise restarting everolimus.

logistics.title: Radiotherapy or surgery
logistics.text: Tell both teams that you take everolimus. Treatment given during or soon after radiotherapy may increase toxicity, and previous irradiated areas can develop recall inflammation. The teams decide spacing or interruption; there is no universal interval on this card.

logistics.title: Response scans
logistics.text: Ask which scan will assess benefit and when it is due. Routine response imaging follows your individual plan. New breathing symptoms need earlier assessment rather than waiting for that scan.

support.title: Nausea support
support.text: NCCP classifies everolimus as minimal-to-low emetic risk. There are no routine infusion premedications. Any as-needed antiemetic follows the individual prescription and local oral-SACT policy.

support.title: Prevent and treat mouth soreness
support.text: Discuss non-alcoholic mouth care and a prescribed alcohol-free corticosteroid mouthwash during the first eight weeks. Avoid irritating products containing alcohol, hydrogen peroxide, iodine or thyme derivatives. Check for oral thrush; do not automatically add an antifungal.

support.title: Steroids and infection prevention
support.text: Systemic steroids may be needed for pneumonitis. When steroids or other immunosuppressive medicines are used, the team considers PJP prevention; it is not an automatic prescription for every patient.

support.title: Glucose, lipids and bone health
support.text: Manage diabetes and lipid abnormalities alongside treatment. Bone-health advice and medicines depend on fracture risk, DXA findings, diet and vitamin-D status.

support.title: Medicine and supplement review
support.text: Check prescriptions, over-the-counter medicines and supplements with oncology pharmacy. Avoid grapefruit and St John’s wort; some antibiotics and antifungals can markedly change everolimus exposure.

agents.name: Everolimus
agents.explanation: Everolimus binds the intracellular protein FKBP12; this complex inhibits mTORC1, affecting protein synthesis and growth signalling. This pathway can support endocrine resistance, which explains pairing it with an oestrogen-lowering medicine. The same pathway operates in normal tissues, contributing to mouth ulcers, infection risk and metabolic changes.
agents.watch: Report new mouth soreness, cough/breathlessness, fever/infection symptoms, diarrhoea or excessive thirst promptly. A new cough must not simply be labelled drug pneumonitis without checking other causes.
risks: Impaired wound healing and radiation-related toxicity

agents.name: Exemestane
agents.mechanism: Irreversibly inhibits aromatase and lowers oestrogen production
agents.explanation: After menopause, aromatase in tissues converts androgen precursors into oestrogen. Exemestane is an irreversible aromatase inhibitor that reduces this supply to hormone-sensitive cancer cells. It does not directly switch off functioning ovaries; the menopausal indication must be confirmed.
agents.watch: Tell the team if joint pain, hot flushes, vaginal dryness or sleep disturbance affects daily life. Bone thinning can be silent, so keep the agreed bone-health reviews.

anatomy: Often develops early; report ulcers before eating or drinking becomes difficult.
Prompt assessment is needed for pneumonitis, infection and other causes.
Changes may be silent; keep blood-test appointments and report marked thirst or frequent urination.
Report persistent diarrhoea, inability to drink or dehydration.
Joint symptoms can affect activity; bone loss needs risk-based monitoring.

evidence.title: BOLERO-2 final progression-free survival analysis
evidence.population: 724 postmenopausal patients with HR-positive/HER2-negative advanced breast cancer after non-steroidal aromatase inhibitors; everolimus+exemestane versus placebo+exemestane.
evidence.primary_endpoint: Investigator-assessed PFS: median 7.8 versus 3.2 months; HR 0.45 (95% CI 0.38–0.54), p<0.0001. Central review: 11.0 versus 4.1 months.
evidence.interpretation: Adding mTOR inhibition delayed progression compared with exemestane alone in this trial population.
evidence.limitations: Conducted before routine CDK4/6-inhibitor use; the observed benefit is not a guaranteed individual outcome and is not direct randomised evidence for current post-CDK4/6 sequencing.

evidence.title: BOLERO-2 overall survival analysis
evidence.population: Same randomised BOLERO-2 population; overall survival was a key secondary endpoint.
evidence.primary_endpoint: Overall survival: median 31.0 versus 26.6 months; HR 0.89 (95% CI 0.73–1.10), p=0.14.
evidence.interpretation: No statistically significant overall-survival advantage was demonstrated. Do not present the PFS benefit as proven longer survival.
evidence.limitations: Subsequent therapies were common; OS was secondary, and the confidence interval includes no difference.

evidence.title: SWISH stomatitis-prevention study
evidence.population: Single-arm prevention study in 92 postmenopausal women starting everolimus+exemestane; 85 evaluable for the week 8 stomatitis endpoint in the EU SmPC report.
evidence.primary_endpoint: EU SmPC reports Grade ≥2 stomatitis at 8 weeks in 2/85 (2.4%); no Grade 3/4 cases.
evidence.interpretation: Supports discussing a prescribed alcohol-free dexamethasone mouthwash early in treatment. Study regimen: 0.5 mg/5 mL solution, 10 mL swished for 2 minutes and spat four times daily for 8 weeks; local formulation/prescribing review is needed.
evidence.limitations: Single-arm study with historical comparison, not a randomised concurrent control; oral candidiasis occurred and the mouthwash is a separate prescription.

clinical_notes: NCCP 00322 is not an exemestane monotherapy card and not an adjuvant endocrine regimen; do not inherit those eligibility lists.
The old encoding had only two generic rules and no operative ANC/platelet or detailed toxicity decisions. This audit adds 77 source-linked rules with component-specific actions.
NCCP Table 3 uses CTCAE v3.0. Do not infer its metabolic/stomatitis grade solely from a generic CTCAE v5 label.
For grade 3 febrile neutropenia, the NCCP restart ANC is ≥1.25×10^9/L with no fever, different from the afebrile neutropenia threshold ≥1.
Exemestane continues through everolimus interruption or modification unless a separate clinical reason changes the plan.
Child-Pugh A/B/C: NCCP everolimus 75%/50%/25% of original dose. EU SmPC adds benefit-risk qualification and 2.5 mg/day maximum for Child-Pugh C. No automatic combined hepatic/toxicity restart dose.
No automatic imaging schedule is invented. The clinical team must define the response-assessment plan; pulmonary symptoms warrant urgent investigation.
Radiotherapy is not a routine phase of this regimen. Show any actual radiotherapy on a parallel individual plan, with an explicit joint decision about everolimus timing.

Independent clinical and oncology-pharmacy validation remains pending. The current-catalogue NCCP v4 PDF and EMA product information (updated 20 November 2025) were downloaded and cross-checked, with visual review of their toxicity tables.
